author: blu
body: The other end. `Works chapter WorkServer` answers "give me the work with hash X" and nothing has ever asked it, because nothing listens. This listens.

author: blu
body: The index is built ONCE, before the loop. Rebuilding it per request would re-read the whole fact log for every quotation.

author: blu
body: The reply carries a `from`, and nobody checks it -- `accept-reply` ignores it, because the reply is answerable by its own content. It is filled in honestly anyway: a fixed tool key, the same shape `cdx-store` signs with. A deployment serves under the box's own identity.

author: blu
body: A tag that is not a work request is dropped rather than answered. `serve-work` is the only verb this binary offers, so a peer that framed something else at it gets nothing back and the connection closes.

author: blu
body: The renewal poll is deliberately short. This runs between connections on a service loop, so a renewal that polled the way the acquisition does would stall answering for as long as it took to give up.

author: blu
body: A renewal is reported only when it moved the lease, so a quiet server does not print a line per pass. The comparison is on lease-start, which is the field an accepted ACK writes and the one an unanswered renewal leaves alone.
